rounds.text: iStreet Network Ltd currently trades at a significant valuation premium, with a P/E ratio of 80.4x and a P/B ratio of 6.91x, both of which vastly exceed their respective sector benchmarks [E1, E2, E6, E7]. This aggressive pricing is further challenged by a discounted cash flow analysis that suggests an intrinsic value of only Rs 23 per share, implying a -100% margin of safety at the current market price [E39, E40]. The company’s financial health is undermined by negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -35 Cr and Rs -42 Cr respectively, leading to a concerning cash conversion ratio of -7.00x [E29, E30, E31]. Furthermore, the significant reduction in promoter holding from 46.20% to 16.58% signals a lack of long-term commitment from insiders [E37, E55, E56]. Operational efficiency is also under pressure, as evidenced by high debtor days of 365 and an increase in working capital days from 77.8 to 143 [E57, E58]. Conceded: the company maintains a strong balance sheet with no debt [E33, E35] and has demonstrated impressive compounded sales and profit growth over recent periods [E15, E18].
